top.provisionalName: Cyclic oligonucleotide signaling hubs (CBASS / Thoeris / Pycsar class)

mostSurprisingArchitecture.provisionalName: Cyclic oligonucleotide signaling hubs (CBASS / Thoeris / Pycsar class)
mostSurprisingArchitecture.statement: Second-messenger cyclic oligonucleotide immune hubs (CBASS / Thoeris / Pycsar class): infection state is encoded into a small-molecule message that triggers cell-fate effectors. Conventional annotation often lists polymerase and effector ORFs separately; the unified sensor→encode→respond architecture is still under-recognized relative to CRISPR spacer memory.
mostSurprisingArchitecture.whyNotCrisprLookalike: Lead is chosen for under-explained information-flow architecture, not resemblance to DNA cutting.
mostSurprisingArchitecture.confidence: medium–high literature; medium as "under-recognized unified mechanism"

novelTestablePrediction.prediction: Separable polymerase-dead vs effector-dead alleles will produce opposite molecular signatures under matched MOI: polymerase-dead → no cyclic messenger accumulation and no abortive phenotype; effector-dead → messenger accumulates without cell-fate change. This double dissociation is not entailed by “find another CRISPR-like cutter” search criteria and falsifies a pure nuclease-centric model of the cassette.

ranked.provisionalName: Cyclic oligonucleotide signaling hubs (CBASS / Thoeris / Pycsar class)
ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: Each system is a standalone abortive-infection gadget; no need for a cross-system information architecture.
ranked.falsificationTest: If polymerase-dead alleles retain effector activation without messenger, the encode-step collapses.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: Messenger accumulates after infection-relevant cues and is required for effector engagement.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Polymerase KO: sensing without abortive phenotype; effector KO: messenger accumulates without cell-fate change.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Separable polymerase/effector alleles + messenger LC-MS + phage fitness under controlled MOI.
ranked.confidence: medium–high literature; medium as "under-recognized unified mechanism"
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Would elevate second-messenger encoding as a prokaryotic information architecture peer — or predecessor in abstraction — to spacer memory.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: High as unified architecture recognition: the surprising object is the *messenger encode step*, not another nuclease.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Viral-state sensor → polymerase synthesizes cyclic oligonucleotide second messenger → effector binds messenger → cell-fate response (often abortive)
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: Polymerases, effectors, and accessory ORFs are frequently annotated as separate hypotheticals; the messenger is invisible to gene-name pipelines.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (cOS / CD-NTase) · genetic (operon neighborhoods) · cellular (suicide / dormancy) · population (phage suppression) · evolutionary (convergent messenger chemistries)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Transient infection state encoded into a small-molecule message that triggers a stereotyped effector program.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Short-lived messenger memory of recent sensing; some systems couple to durable downstream states.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Cell fate removes infected hosts from the productive phage pool.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Population-level viability band under phage pressure via sacrificial cells.
ranked.knownExplanations: CBASS/Thoeris literature describes messenger chemistry and effectors; still under-taught as a *general* sensor→encode→respond class outside specialist circles.

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: DGRs are already explained as localized hypermutation gadgets; no broader principle required.
ranked.falsificationTest: If VR diversity is indistinguishable from local mutation hotspots without template dependence, the templated-engine claim fails.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: Template–VR pairing and RT dependence are required for localized nonsynonymous spikes.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Loss of RT collapses tip diversity and reduces adaptation speed under fluctuating partners.
ranked.minimumExperiment: RT knockout + deep VR sequencing under controlled partner fluctuation vs template-intact controls.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Would show biology can *write future diversity* on purpose — not only remember past invaders — a different information job than CRISPR.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: High as a *unified information-processing* framing: directed rewrite for future matching, not spacer storage of past invaders.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Reverse transcriptase + template RNA/DNA + target gene variable region → directed, mutagenic rewrite that diversifies a protein tip without rewriting the whole gene
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: RT, VR, and accessory ORFs are often annotated separately; co-occurrence without a cutter label looks like junk or phage debris.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (error-prone RT) · genetic (cassette) · cellular (surface/receptor diversity) · population (escape / adhesion variants) · evolutionary (recurrent cassette architecture)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Prior selective pressure is hypothesized to condition which diversified variants persist; template guides *where* diversity is written.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Template region preserves a reference while VR accumulates directed changes.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Successful variants alter future host–virus or adhesion outcomes.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Diversification can keep a viable matching band under shifting partners — dynamic, not static.
ranked.knownExplanations: Diversity-generating retroelements are published; often framed as niche mutagenesis, not as a general information architecture peer to CRISPR memory.

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.falsificationTest: If mark erasure does not change subsequent response probabilities, memory claim fails for that locus.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: Mark occupancy predicts later expression under matched cues.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Timed cue + ChIP/methylome + expression with writer KO.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Establishes non-sequence genomic memory as a core answer class.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Low as novelty; high as multi-scale recurrence peer for the discovery question.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Environmental/developmental cue → chromatin mark / DNA methylation / histone state → retained representation → altered future transcription
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: Marks, writers, readers, erasers annotated as separate enzymatic families; the *state tape* is relational.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (marks) · genomic (loci) · cellular (expression memory) · organism (development/immunity) · population (plasticity)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Cue → encode as chromatin state → store across division → gate later response.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Mitotic and some transgenerational mark retention (taxon-dependent).
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Expression changes alter metabolism and further marking.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Keeps expression in viable bands under fluctuating cues.
ranked.knownExplanations: Vast epigenetics literature; SING13 Soft Story peers exist (histone / phase-lock papers).

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: Pathology-only misfolding — not adaptive information processing.
ranked.falsificationTest: If conformational propagation never alters subsequent adaptive response probabilities, drop the learning claim.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: Seeded misfold fraction predicts phenotype switch rate.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Seeding changes trait distribution without DNA mutation.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Controlled seeding + phenotype assay + sequencing to exclude DNA change.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Breaks the assumption that consequential biological memory must look like CRISPR.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Moderate as *non-nucleic* memory peer — important falsifier of "must be DNA cutting" bias.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Protein conformational state templates identical folds → propagates a non-nucleic representation of prior state → alters phenotype
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: Treated as pathology or yeast epigenetics; rarely filed beside CRISPR as information architecture.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (fold) · cellular (phenotype switch) · organism (disease/trait) · evolutionary (rare stable states)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Prior fold state encodes information that templates future folds.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Conformational inheritance without DNA sequence change.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Phenotype can reinforce conditions favoring the fold.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Usually pathological; some yeast prions act as bet-hedging switches.
ranked.knownExplanations: Prion biology is published; SING13 Soft Story peer exists (prion-refold paper).

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: Fully explained germline TE defense — not an unrecognized architecture.
ranked.falsificationTest: If cluster content does not predict silencing specificity, memory claim fails.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: piRNA matches track TE families present in recent history.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Cluster edit + TE expression + piRNA-seq in germline models.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Animal-scale genomic memory peer for the core discovery question.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Low–moderate as mechanism; moderate as multi-scale *genomic memory* peer often omitted from prokaryotic CRISPR comparisons.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Transposon encounter → piRNA cluster encoding → piRNA guides → silencing of matching TEs → feedback into cluster content over generations
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: piRNA biogenesis, TE fragments, and silencing proteins are siloed across genomics and developmental biology annotations.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (piRNA) · genomic (clusters) · cellular (silencing) · organism (germline defense) · evolutionary (TE–host arms race)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Prior TE sequence content retained as RNA guides that alter future TE activity.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Cluster content is heritable sequence memory of TE families.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Silencing success changes TE load and subsequent cluster evolution.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Keeps TE activity in a viable band for germline integrity.
ranked.knownExplanations: piRNA pathway is extensively published in animals.

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: Retrons are adequately explained as toxin-linked defense modules without needing a higher-order information theory.
ranked.falsificationTest: If msDNA production is dispensable for the linked phenotype, the encode-step claim fails.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: msDNA abundance tracks cassette activation under phage-relevant stress.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: RT-dead alleles lose defense without losing neighboring toxin genes.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Allelic RT vs toxin separation + phage plaque assays + msDNA quantification.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Shows DNA writing as an intermediate representation — not only cleavage — in prokaryotic information flow.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Moderate–high as distributed writer architecture; not a novel enzyme class claim.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Reverse transcriptase produces multicopy single-stranded DNA products from structured RNA; neighborhood proteins couple products to defense or regulatory outcomes
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: msDNA and RT often filed as curiosities; recent defense links are still fragmented across annotation pipelines.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (RT / msDNA) · genetic (retron cassettes) · cellular (abortive / toxic response) · population (phage selection)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Structured RNA → DNA product as an encoded intermediate that can gate downstream effectors.
ranked.evidenceMemory: msDNA can persist as a molecular product reflecting cassette state.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Defense activation alters survival under phage load.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Abortive infection trades cell death for population protection.
ranked.knownExplanations: Retrons explained as msDNA producers; phage-defense coupling increasingly documented.

ranked.provisionalName: Integron cassette capture as adaptive genomic encoding
ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: Plain HGT accumulation — no need for information-architecture language.
ranked.falsificationTest: If cassette order/content does not change subsequent response probabilities under matched stress, drop the learning claim.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: Recent stress-associated cassettes appear near the attI expression pole more often than null models.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Integrase-dead strains freeze repertoire and lose adaptive acquisition speed.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Controlled cassette challenge + array sequencing + MIC / stress assays vs IntI KO.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Would show genomic learning via cassette grammar without CRISPR-like spacers — unexpected relative to cutter-centric search.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Moderate: known HGT machine, under-recognized as sensor-agnostic *genomic learning* architecture.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Environmental gene cassettes → site-specific recombination into integron array → ordered expression potential → alters future antimicrobial / stress responses
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: Integrases and cassettes annotated; the *ordered encoding of prior encounters with mobile genes* is under-framed as learning.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (IntI) · genetic (att sites) · genomic (arrays) · cellular (expression) · population (HGT ecology)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Prior cassette acquisition encodes encounter history that changes subsequent resistance repertoire.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Array content is durable genomic memory of acquired cassettes.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Expression and selection reshape which cassettes persist.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Expands response repertoire under antibiotic/stress regimes.
ranked.knownExplanations: Integron literature is established in antibiotic resistance.

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: Well-known stress / Abi modules — no new architecture.
ranked.falsificationTest: If toxin activation is uncorrelated with infection-relevant cues, the sensing claim fails.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: Antitoxin depletion coincides with infection markers.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Toxin KO increases phage burst size.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Timed infection + antitoxin stability + plaque assays.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Clarifies population-level homeostasis as information flow without genomic writing.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Low–moderate; useful as homeostasis peer, weak as unrecognized architecture.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Infection or stress tip balance → toxin liberation → cell stall/death → population phage suppression; antitoxin restores viable band
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: TA pairs annotated as stress gadgets; information role at population scale is under-weighted vs molecular labels.
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Local infection state triggers a sacrificial response that changes collective future phage dynamics.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Some TA systems couple to persister states (temporary program memory).
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Abort reduces phage burst; survivors reshape next generation.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Classic deviation→corrective response at colony scale.

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.falsificationTest: If methylation-blind hosts show no specificity change, self-signature memory fails.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Methylase KO increases self-restriction or phage susceptibility patterns.
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Pre-CRISPR nucleic discrimination peer for the queue.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Low–moderate; useful baseline that CRISPR is not the only nucleic defense grammar.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Recognize non-self DNA patterns → cut or guide interference → protect self via methylation or guide RNA; neighborhoods often co-occur with poorly annotated ORFs
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: R-M and pAgo systems annotated as restriction gadgets; poorly characterized neighbors ignored.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular · genetic · cellular · population phage ecology
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Self/non-self discrimination encodes a standing rule that alters future DNA survival.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Methylation state is a standing self-signature (not event chronology like CRISPR).
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Cleavage alters phage success and selection on motifs.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Keeps foreign DNA load in a viable band.

ranked.antiBiasNotes: Survived primary anti-bias floors (still may be fully explained by prior literature).
ranked.strongestCompetingExplanation: CRISPR is already adequately recognized as adaptive immunity — unification adds framing, not a new enzyme class.
ranked.falsificationTest: If spacer arrays do not retain usable prior-state information under controlled serial infection, the memory claim fails.
ranked.predictedMolecularObservation: New spacers map to recent phage genomes; array polarity predicts temporal order.
ranked.predictedBiologicalPhenotype: Prior exposure alters subsequent resistance specificity without requiring protein-only memory.
ranked.minimumExperiment: Serial phage challenge + spacer sequencing + interference assay vs naïve controls.
ranked.confidence: high (known mechanism); low as "beyond CRISPR" novelty
ranked.significanceIfTrue: Baseline: proves biology already implements sensor→encode→store→compare→respond — the search must look *past* cutter novelty.
ranked.noveltyAssessment: Low as a named cutter; moderate as a *general* biological information-processing template that other systems may echo.
ranked.observedArchitecture: Sensor (foreign nucleic acid) → encode (spacer acquisition) → store (CRISPR array) → compare (crRNA guide) → response (cleavage/interference) → feedback (primed acquisition)
ranked.whyAnnotationMisses: Well annotated as adaptive immunity; often treated as a cutter toolkit rather than a general state→encode→store→compare→respond architecture.
ranked.multiScalePattern: Molecular (Cas proteins) · genetic (cas operon + repeats) · genomic (arrays) · cellular (interference) · population (phage–host coevolution)
ranked.possibleInformationFlow: Prior infection state written into spacer order; subsequent encounters use stored guides.
ranked.evidenceMemory: Spacer arrays retain chronological infection history in many systems.
ranked.evidenceFeedback: Primed acquisition and autoimmunity avoidance loops.
ranked.evidenceHomeostasis: Abortive outcomes and regulated expression tune host viability under phage pressure.
ranked.knownExplanations: Mature CRISPR literature explains spacer acquisition, interference, and regulation in detail.
